llc.formation_notes: Statute: $45 when filed online, $100 on paper (RSMo 347.179). The Secretary of State site (sos.mo.gov) blocks automated reading, so any added online processing fee was not checked.

annual_report.name: None
annual_report.due: Missouri LLCs file no annual report

sources.title: RSMo 347.179 LLC filing fees
sources.quote: For filing the original articles of organization online, in an electronic format prescribed by the secretary of state, a fee of forty-five dollars

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: SALT Parity Act (RSMo 143.436): electing partnership or S corp pays tax on Missouri net income at the highest individual rate (4.7% for 2026 per withholding formula); members get a credit. Election made each year on Form MO-PTE.

sources.title: RSMo 143.436 SALT Parity Act
sources.quote: shall be multiplied by the highest rate of tax used to determine a Missouri income tax liability for an individual pursuant to section 143.011

personal_exemption.notes: No personal exemption. Same brackets for all filing statuses. Standard deduction equals the federal standard deduction (RSMo 143.131).

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: None. From tax year 2025, 100% of capital gains reported by individuals is subtracted (RSMo 143.121.3(14)).

sources.title: USDA National Finance Center bulletin reproducing the Missouri 2026 withholding formula
RSMo 143.131
sources.quote: The Missouri standard deduction shall be the allowable federal standard deduction.

sources.title: RSMo 143.121
sources.quote: For all tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, one hundred percent of all income reported as a capital gain for federal income tax purposes by an individual

sources.title: RSMo 143.011 (rate cuts, indexing)
sources.quote: the brackets of Missouri taxable income identified in subsection 1 of this section shall be adjusted annually by the percent increase in inflation.

estimated_tax.required_if: Missouri estimated tax reasonably expected to be at least $100
estimated_tax.notes: Due dates follow the federal schedule (not read on dor.mo.gov, which blocks automated access).

unemployment_2026.notes: labor.mo.gov blocks automated reading. Secondary sources report $9,000 wage base and 2.376% new employer rate (1% nonprofits) for 2026 - not verified.

local_taxes.name: Earnings tax (profits tax on net profits, Form RD-108)
local_taxes.applies: residents on all earnings and net profits; nonresidents on earnings/net profits from work or business in Kansas City; sole proprietors, partnerships and corporations file RD-108 on net profits
local_taxes.quote: Form RD-108/108B is a tax return used by a sole proprietor, corporation, partnership ... to file and pay the earnings tax of 1% due on net profits.

local_taxes.name: Earnings tax (individual E-1 / business E-234)
local_taxes.applies: residents regardless of where they work, nonresidents working in the City; businesses (incl. self-employed and sole proprietors) on business earnings
local_taxes.quote: All businesses located in the City of St. Louis, except those exempted by law, are required to pay the earnings tax of 1% of the business's earnings.

local_taxes.name: Payroll expense tax (Form P-10)
local_taxes.applies: employers on compensation paid for work in the City (relevant to an S corp paying its owner a salary)
local_taxes.quote: The Payroll Expense Tax is a 0.5% tax paid by the employer for wages earned in the City of St. Louis.

notable: No annual report and a $45 online formation fee make Missouri one of the cheapest LLC states (https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=347.179)
Kansas City and St. Louis each levy a 1% earnings tax that also hits self-employment net profits (https://www.kcmo.gov/city-hall/departments/finance/tax-home/tax-form-descriptions)
Capital gains fully exempt for individuals from 2025 (https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=143.121)
Top rate 4.7% starts at only $9,436 of taxable income in 2026 (https://help.nfc.usda.gov/bulletins/2026/1773783048.htm)
uncertain: dor.mo.gov, sos.mo.gov and labor.mo.gov block automated access (Incapsula/Cloudflare). 2026 brackets and standard deduction were read from the USDA National Finance Center's reproduction of the Missouri DOR 2026 withholding formula, not from DOR directly; they match RSMo 143.131 (federal standard deduction).
Whether a further 0.1-point top-rate cut applies for 2026 was not read on DOR; withholding formula uses 4.70%.
SUTA 2026 wage base and new employer rate not verified on an official page.
Possible SOS online processing surcharge over the $45 statutory fee not verified.
